title: Action de Galois sur Teichmüller : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, from the previous page: X is a K-scheme of finite type (K a subfield of C, typically a number field). Π_1(X) is the topological fundamental groupoid of X(C), with all points as objects. Π̂_1(X) is its profinite completion, i.e. the étale fundamental groupoid, which has a purely algebraic definition. The big group Aut(C/K) (written Π, or a tilde/bold Γ, in the manuscript) acts on Π̂_1(X). Γ = Gal(K̄/K) acts on the full subgroupoid Π̂_1(X_K̄) on the algebraic points, and the big group acts through the quotient Γ.

This page sets up explicit coordinates for that action. It uses as 'generators' of the profinite groupoid the discrete (topological) paths l : x → y coming from Π_1. For such l, ^u l : ^u x → ^u y is in general only a profinite path.

Grothendieck then restricts to K-rational base points, i.e. the full subgroupoid Π̂_1(X_K) on Γ-invariant objects. There ^u x = x and ^u y = y, so ^u l is again a path x → y. Comparing it with l gives two loops:
- g_l(u) = ^u l · l^{-1}, an element of π̂_1(X, y);
- f_l(u) = l^{-1} · ^u l, an element of π̂_1(X, x).
They satisfy ^u l = g_l(u) ∘ l = l ∘ f_l(u). The two loops determine each other by transport along l: g_l(u) = l f_l(u) l^{-1} and f_l(u) = l^{-1} g_l(u) l. A marginal note introduces the dual notation f_u(l), g_u(l), viewing them for fixed u as functions of the path l.

The programme stated at the bottom: describe the action of u ∈ Γ on a full subgroupoid by the values f_l(u), g_l(u) for a convenient generating system of paths. The next page takes a finite set I of rational points, a base point x_0, paths l_x from x_0 to each x, and generators of π_1(X, x_0). It records the groupoid-cocycle rule g_{l''l'}(u) = g_{l''}(u) · l''(g_{l'}(u)). It also asks whether, e.g. for anabelian curves, the action on Π̂_1(X_K, I) determines u.

In modern terms this is the standard description of the Galois action on the étale fundamental groupoid with several rational base points by a non-abelian 'path cocycle'. Ihara's f_σ for P^1 − {0,1,∞} (with tangential base points) and Drinfeld's GT-parametrisation are exactly this construction. Here it is written for genuine rational base points.
errors: No mathematical error on this page. The formulas (8)/(9) are consistent with right-to-left composition: g_l(u) = ^u l l^{-1} is a loop at y and f_l(u) = l^{-1} ^u l is a loop at x. The next page's cocycle rule g_{l''l'} = g_{l''} · l''(g_{l'}) checks out.

Gap: restricting to K-rational points is vacuous for the key example P^1 − {0,1,∞}, which has no K-rational points off the punctures. That case needs tangential base points (Deligne) or points at infinity; the page does not address this.
Gap: the dependence on u is not recorded here. One has g_l(uv) = u(g_l(v)) · g_l(u), a twisted cocycle in u. Only the multiplicativity in the path variable appears, on the next page.

ideas.what: Galois action on the étale fundamental groupoid with several base points, coordinatised by loops f_l(u) = l^{-1}·^u l attached to topological paths l between rational points
ideas.modern_name: Galois path cocycle / Ihara's f_σ, Drinfeld–Ihara parametrisation of G_Q in GT; Galois action on étale path torsors π̂_1(X; x, y)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara (1985–86, f_σ for P^1−{0,1,∞}); Deligne (1989, tangential base points, path torsors); Drinfeld (1990, GT)
ideas.where_published: The Esquisse d'un programme (1984) discusses Teichmüller groupoids with several base points and the Galois action on them in prose. The explicit f_l(u)/g_l(u) formalism is not there to my knowledge.

ideas.what: Transport between the two loop-valued invariants, g_l(u) = l f_l(u) l^{-1}, and the non-abelian cocycle law in the path variable (next page)
ideas.modern_name: groupoid 1-cocycle / crossed-homomorphism condition for path torsors
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard non-abelian cohomology; in this context Ihara, Deligne

ideas.what: Using the discrete topological groupoid Π_1 as a dense set of 'generators' of the profinite groupoid in order to describe the Galois action
ideas.modern_name: comparison isomorphism between the profinite completion of the topological π_1 and the étale π_1; choosing topological paths to coordinatise the Galois action
ideas.usually_credited_to: SGA1 (Grothendieck) for the comparison; standard in Ihara's and Deligne's work

missed.claim: This is an early (≥1978, plausibly pre-Ihara 1985) private formulation of the Galois-on-groupoid path cocycle, using two-sided invariants f_l(u), g_l(u) and the dual notation f_u(l) as a function on paths. The construction itself is now standard and credited to Ihara, Deligne and Drinfeld. Its interest is only as a priority/historical detail, not as a new result.
missed.quote: ^u l = g_l(u)∘l = l∘f_l(u), g_l(u) ∈ Π̂_1(X,y), f_l(u) ∈ Π̂_1(X,x)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents that Grothendieck had the explicit cocycle formalism for the multi-base-point Galois action before the published Ihara/Deligne treatments. This matters for histories of Grothendieck–Teichmüller theory, not for current research.

deep.surprise_reason: A clean but routine setup page. The path-cocycle description of the Galois action on the étale fundamental groupoid is now textbook (Ihara, Deligne, Drinfeld). The possible early date is mildly interesting historically, but the page contains no result absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: the group written 'Π' (in 'u∈Π') is very likely Grothendieck's symbol for the larger group Aut(C/K), perhaps a decorated Γ, of which Γ = Gal(K̄/K) is a quotient (cf. previous page). It is not the fundamental groupoid Π_1.
The margin note reads approximately 'On écrira aussi f_u(l), g_u(l) au lieu de f_l(u), g_l(u)' (diagonal, left margin). The sense is correct in the transcription.
In (8), the struck-out text after 'l∘f_l(u)' appears to be a crossed-out alternative notation (something like 'f_l(u), g_l(u)'), not mathematics.
The page number at the bottom left is 69 (the manuscript's own numbering), consistent with the archive position.
